description:
Hi everyone! 

I'm building IGNIS for NASA Space Apps 2026, an AI-powered platform exploring fire-safety insights from NASA's microgravity combustion data.
I bring skills in Python, React, FastAPI, and AI/ML. 
Looking for collaborators interested in RAG, UI/UX, data science, physics, or space research. 

Experienced or beginner, let's connect, combine our strengths, and build something amazing together!
summary: FLARE-X is a web platform that makes NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to search, compare and trust. Fire behaves very differently in space, but the findings are scattered across catalogue entries. We organised 24 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Combustion Science investigations into an interactive workspace: an Investigation Explorer, side-by-side comparison, transparent relevance ranking by theme (detection, prevention, suppression), an evidence-gap view, and an evidence-linked Research Assistant. Every answer shows the PSI records it came from. Where data is missing, FLARE-X says "Not available in the provided source" instead of guessing. The assistant works without AI and can optionally use Gemini behind guardrails that check citations and numbers. FLARE-X helps researchers and engineers quickly see what is known, what is missing, and where to look next for spacecraft fire safety.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FLARE-X turns a snapshot of 24 NASA PSI Combustion Science investigations (19 microgravity, 5 ground) into an interactive research workspace. Users can search and filter investigations, compare two or three side by side, rank them by research theme with an explainable keyword score, see which metadata fields are captured versus missing, and ask questions to an evidence-linked Research Assistant. The assistant offers three workflows: cited Q&A, cross-investigation comparison, and research-brief generation.

HOW IT WORKS

A FastAPI backend validates and serves the catalogue. A React + Vite frontend presents it. The assistant is retrieval-first: it fetches the relevant PSI records, then answers with those records shown as evidence. It works fully without AI. If a Gemini key is configured server-side, Gemini output is checked against the retrieved evidence for unsupported citations and invented numbers, and the system safely falls back to catalogue answers (reporting a fallback reason) if checks fail. The response always states which mode actually ran.

WHY IT MATTERS

Fire in microgravity is a real spacecraft safety concern, yet existing research is hard to survey quickly. FLARE-X shortens the path from "what has been studied?" to "what is missing?", making gaps in the evidence visible.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN CHOICES

- Honesty first: missing values are never shown as zero or filled in; rankings are labelled as software interpretations, not NASA classifications or safety scores.

- A 3D Three.js "evidence flow" visual explains how data moves through the platform.

- A citation audit page shows which DOIs were individually verified (6) and which still need checking (18).

- Secrets stay server-side; 39 backend and 14 frontend tests pass; deployed via Docker on Render.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Three.js, Lucide icons, Docker, Render, GitHub Actions, optional Google Gemini API.

LIMITS

FLARE-X uses catalogue metadata only. It is not raw experimental data, full-text paper analysis, or a spacecraft fire-risk model, and it does not imply NASA endorsement.

Source code: https://github.com/DishaB-07/FLARE-X
